name: Alexander Robinson, trader of St. Joseph, perhaps at Chicago in August 1812

The card states what its sources say, with their tier, and stages no speech, ceremony or act of war.

persons.name: Alexander Robinson (Che-che-pin-qua)

present_on_scene_date.note: The sources disagree whether he was here on the 14th.

persons.note: A trader from St. Joseph, born at Mackinac to an Odawa mother and a Scottish father, by popular belief in 1762. Whether he was at Chicago in August 1812 the sources do not agree: Andreas has him arrive too late to stop the killing yet a witness to it; Quaife names him among the chiefs; Wau-Bun puts him only at St. Joseph afterwards, where he sheltered the Kinzies, and with his wife he paddled the Healds to Mackinac. He was later a chief of the united Potawatomi, Chippewa and Ottawa and signed the 1833 treaty, kept a reservation on the Des Plaines, and died there on 22 April 1872.
